html:
Guatemala is the most populous country of Central America, and the heartland of the Maya, who still make up a large part of its people. It has been a separate republic since 1839.

Great Maya cities such as Tikal rose in its northern forests. The K'iche' Maya of the highlands later wrote down their sacred story, the Popol Vuh. Pedro de Alvarado conquered the highlands for Spain in 1524, and Guatemala became the seat of Spanish rule over all of Central America. After independence in 1821 the conservative strongman Rafael Carrera led it out of the Central American federation.

In the years the map shows from 1880:

  • Liberal governments from 1871 pushed coffee growing and forced Maya villagers to work on the estates.
  • Dictators such as Jorge Ubico gave American companies, above all the United Fruit Company, vast land and power.
  • A revolution in 1944 brought elected governments. President Jacobo Árbenz began a land reform that took unused land from United Fruit.
  • The coup of 1954, organised by the CIA, overthrew Árbenz.

The coup led to the civil war of 1960 to 1996, which killed about 200,000 people. In the early 1980s the army destroyed hundreds of Maya villages in what a UN-backed truth commission later called genocide. The Maya activist Rigoberta Menchú won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992, and peace accords were signed in 1996. Guatemala long claimed neighbouring Belize.
sum: Guatemala is the most populous country of Central America, and the heartland of the Maya, who still make up a large part of its people. It has been a separate republic since 1839.
